status: LIVE design data v4: the vertical slice (milestones M1, M2a and M2b; survival_gdd.md version 4). The game and tests/survival/test_survival_data.gd read these rows. Every number is tunable.
summary: Backgrounds are head starts: the backcountry hunter (M1) and the discharged provincial or ranger (M2a), each with starting levels, kit, a little money, known recipes, people and a habit any character can earn. Debts are optional start variants; the default start owes nothing.
id_rules: Ids are stable strings (prefix.name). Never rename an id once saves exist; add an alias instead. Display names are separate and may change. An id is defined in exactly one place: the live file or the backlog.

milestones.M1: A winter night: fire, shelter, cold, hunger, sleep, time safety; the fort region only; one background; 1765
milestones.M2a: A winter from the woods: living from the manor woods through the winter by your own hands (gathering, hides, sewing, snares, snowshoes, a half-faced camp, a hung cache, ice fishing); plain barter with the sutler, the trader, the garrison's soldiers, a farm family from German Flatts and an old hunter; credit and the fall outfit as options; the second background
milestones.M2b: Learning from neighbours: lessons, watching, examining, quality standards, haggling, promises and loans
milestones.M3: The year turns: the full almanac, seasons and weather content, the summer goal (bark and a cabin), fishing, frogs, ginseng, one played wage job; the fur cap and robe, leggings, carving, casting balls, the cache pit, char cloth and spruce beer
milestones.M4: People: NPC schedules and tiers at the fort, standing, invitations, the soldiers and the lieutenant as mentors; Native characters only after the relevant nation's sign-off
milestones.M5: The map: the Carry, the valley, the town and the hunting grounds, travel and camps, other markets and backgrounds
milestones.post: After M5 and not yet planned: the 1757 and 1761 starts and their eras, detailed illnesses, thirst, potash, upstream canoe and bateau travel, the Proxy NPC tier, languages beyond English, French, Mohawk and Oneida

rules: A background is a head start: starting skill levels, kit, a little money, known recipes, people and a habit any character can earn. It never locks a skill, recipe or action, and gives no experience multiplier (redesign_skills.md rules L1 and L7).
Skill budgets are 145-155 over the ten live skills, none above 35 at the start, and each background spikes in a different livelihood that is live in the default era (1765).
Every habit touches a system the slice has (listed in touches; tested), and any character earns it by doing.
Debts are optional start variants chosen at creation (start_variants); the default, Clear, owes nothing.
Outfits are cosmetic: an outfit set only suggests a background; any outfit goes with any background.

Nothing is locked by sex. Where a period institution was male-only (militia rolls, provincial and ranging service), obligation_rules give the historical equivalent, or the documented-fiction option applies.
No stat is tied to ancestry or ethnicity.

skill_budget.rule: sum of starting levels over the ten live skills; no skill above 35 at the start

historical.men: answer the district's musters and alarms (event.militia_muster)
historical.women: supply the muster (provisions worth 60 d), or in an alarm hold the blockhouse or lodge refugee families; same standing effects

militia.service_history: Provincial and ranging service was men's service; women followed regiments on the ration list as wives, laundresses and nurses, and some kept sutlers' stores. Default: a woman takes the ration-list variant.
militia.open_musters: Option: anyone may answer musters and take any service history. Documented as deliberate fiction.

creation_flow: 2. Background (M1: the backcountry hunter only; M2a: two), then the service variant.
3. Start variant: Clear (default), Outfitted on credit, On the sutler's tally, or (M2b) A promise to keep.
4. Summary of skills, kit, known recipes, people, the habit and any debt or obligation.
5. Start: Early September 1765 at the post at the ford, Woodsman preset by default.

backgrounds.name: Backcountry hunter
backgrounds.life_history: Grew up on the edge of the valley settlements; hunts and traps from fall to spring and lives mostly from the woods, trading skins and furs when the trader comes up the river.
backgrounds.historical_basis: Settler hunters who went out for the season on credit (E:3.3). The term 'long hunter' belonged to southwest Virginia and western North Carolina hunts into Kentucky and Tennessee and is used only at the Ohio node after 1761 (review 1, issue 1).

start.legal_note: Legal. The woods are Cosby's Manor, a 1734 patent surveyed in 1762 and still unsettled (N:33): under colonial practice a hunter needs no one's leave to hunt or trap unenclosed patent land; cutting timber for sale or raising a cabin would need a lease from the proprietors. The Oneida hunting grounds west of the Carry, where leave is needed, come at M5 with their people present.

credit.note: the trader knows him: a full fall outfit

backgrounds.known_note: A backcountry hunter dressed his own skins for moccasins and a hunting shirt, a method learned from Native neighbours (its origin note says so).

backgrounds.name: Discharged provincial or ranger (served 1756-63)
backgrounds.life_history: Served in a New York provincial regiment or a ranging company in the late war (some went on with Bradstreet in 1764), was discharged, and has wintered since at the post. Owes no service to the regulars; like every man of the district he is on the county militia roll.
backgrounds.historical_basis: Provincial service by the campaign season (Anderson, N:10); the ranging companies were disbanded after the war and New York raised no provincials after 1764, so in 1765 a veteran's duty is the county militia, not orders from a commandant (review 1 of v2, blocker).

start.legal_note: Lodges by the sutler's store by the lieutenant's leave; hunts the same manor woods.

choose_one.name: On a regiment's ration list: a soldier's wife, laundress, nurse or sutler's hand, 1756-63
choose_one.note: The historically grounded variant for a woman on the default 'historical' setting.

service.rule: Provincial and ranging service was men's service. On the default 'historical' setting a woman takes the ration-list variant; the 'open service' option lets anyone take any variant and is documented as deliberate fiction (obligation_rules).

credit.note: the trader does not know him yet: a little less

backgrounds.aliases_note: Id kept from v2 (bg.provincial_ranger); the display name and obligation changed in v3.

obligation.fine_note: 48 d in coin or provisions [D]. The v3 draft's work on the fort's works is gone: the regular garrison had no say over the provincial militia's fines [H: verify the colony's militia act]; statute road work is the M5 labour hook (W:13).

backgrounds.seen_note: Seen, not made: steel sets and snowshoes (he wore them), and moccasins, fur mitts and hide dressing (the rangers' winter camps made and mended their own footwear and mittens; fix round 1, F4) [D].

habits.name: Line hand
habits.text: Walks a trap line 20% faster and carries 15% more meat and pelts.

habits.name: Cold camp
habits.text: Campaign camps: sleeps without a fire at 80% of the usual heat loss and raises a brush lean-to in 25% less time.

start_variants.name: Clear
start_variants.text: Owes no one. The background's kit, a little money, the people who know you; arriving between Late November and March, provisions and hooks and line besides.

season_kit.text: Arriving in the cold months, a newcomer brings provisions for the first days (20 lb of cornmeal, 6 lb of salt pork) and hooks and line for the ice [D].

start_variants.name: Outfitted on credit
start_variants.text: Two more steel traps, a pound of powder and a brass kettle on the trader's book: 715 barter d (240 carried from last season), due in the spring window.

start_variants.name: On the sutler's tally
start_variants.text: A pound of powder, four of lead and a blanket on the sutler's tally: 288 d cash, due in the spring window (the v3 debt; her limit rises to 360 d, the balance report's R3).

start_variants.name: A promise to keep
start_variants.text: Promised the sutler 60 lb of venison by Late February for last winter's kindness: kept, +5 garrison standing and her trust; broken, -5.
